gloss: lobe or ridge of the ear
summary: In the ordination of Aaron and his sons, blood is placed on the right ear, thumb and big toe. The cleansing rite in Leviticus 14 marks the same three places with blood and then oil.

words.gloss: lobe or ridge of the ear

senses.gloss: lobe or ridge of the ear
senses.definition: A particular part of the visible ear to which blood or oil is applied. Each occurrence specifies the right ear.

evidence.note: The instruction names the part twice, first for Aaron and then for his sons.
Moses places blood from the ram on Aaron’s ear, thumb and toe.
Moses repeats the action on Aaron’s sons.
The priest places blood from the guilt offering on the ear of the person being cleansed.
Oil is put on the ear over the blood.
The rite for someone of limited means retains the application of blood to the ear.
The oil again goes where the priest applied the blood.

note: The traditional rendering ‘earlobe’ follows the Greek λοβός. Sifra, Metzora 3.5, identifies a middle ridge of the ear. The Hebrew instructions establish the site on the right ear but give no further anatomical description. The oven term filed under the same index key belongs to tannur.
